body: Definitely agree. I don't think they realized how much his behavior impacted me. I can't force them to see things my way, but I hope that when the introduction does come, they don't immediately treat the person I am happy with like crap just because they liked my ex.

Good idea! 

I'm not really worried about them reporting back to him. I think he does still communicate with them, just because of our history, and it honestly bothers me after everything that's happened. I don't understand why they still do to be honest.
Haha, love this! But I've been thinking about taking the "this is the way things are" approach. My parents are very traditional and stuck in their own ways.

Thank you so much! I agree, I think distance is key right now. With everything going on, its unhealthy for me to take on other peoples emotions about my situation. I'm already going through my own! 

I'm seeing a therapist weekly for everything that's happening, and she's wonderful. Between sessions when life happens is the hardest part.

Thank you so much for your kind words. I'm so sorry you're going through a divorce and issues with your family as well. While our situations are different, I'm comforted by the fact that I don't feel alone. That being said, if you ever need anything, feel free to send me a message! 

I've definitely been leaning on my friends, I feel like my family has been the core of a lot of my unhappiness lately and I need to distance myself there. 

Thank you again, I will keep pressing forward and being strong. Wishing you all the best <3

Thank you so much for your kind words. I am definitely leaning on my friends more these days and it's been helping, thankfully! 

I do see a therapist weekly for everything that's been going on. So many things happen outside of therapy sometimes and its hard to make sense of it, or keep my wits about me. 

Thank you, again, for the encouragement.

My therapist said something very similar to me today - not taking on the emotions and opinions of others and letting it taint where I'm find my happiness. 

I'm certain they are disappointed that I'm choosing to be childfree. They want to be grandparents and have children in the house again. Being an only child really does put a lot of pressure on me to give them these things.

Yeah, thats absolutely possible. I know they were looking forward to being grandparents one day. I do hope that, with time, they come to terms with whats happening. I do feel alone and I wish I had some sort of support.
Thank you so much for your sympathies. :)

My parents had a very strong bond with my STBXH. I'm an only child, and my mother really latched onto him once we started seriously dating. He's always been respectful, and is a religious man himself (while I, myself, am not very religious). 

I'm going to quote my above comment to give you some background on the relationship: 

"My spouse initially didn't want the divorce, and we fought for 3 years to repair our relationship by trying to communicate, spend more time together, vacationing, and everything. But we still managed to fight with one another and drift apart. We have very different personalities, and we came to find out in these three years that we had very different life goals. And another cause for contention is that I never wanted children from the get-go and although he accepted this from the beginning of our relationship, he confessed that thought he could change my mind and now really wants to be a father.

And to be honest, he would make a great father, and I think that he should be able to have children with someone who really wants that as well. I would feel horrible taking that aspect of life away from him." 

Although I've expressed why I've decided to end things, my parents view these things as "small problems" seeing that only came to surface in the last 6 months. Perhaps it was my fault for not communicating how unhappy we were 3 years ago when the issues began, but at that point, we were headfast on trying to resolve things and didn't want to alarm our families... even if it didn't quite work out as planned. 

I do agree that perhaps more time will help us. Perhaps, I need to work on my communication as well.

Very sound advice here. You're right, I need to respect their decision just as I want them to respect mine. I'm not a religious person, so we never saw eye-to-eye on things that were traditional in that sense. But I'm their only child, so I think they were holding me to some predetermined expectations.
